when and while

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Emma's story at Jack's.

Grammar Bank2Bwhen and while
the long action (past continuous)the short action (past simple)
whenShe was waiting for a buswhen she saw us.
whileWhile I was taking a photo,my phone ran out of battery.
  • while + the long action (was / were …ing). when usually + the short action (past simple).
  • When the sentence starts with When / While, put a comma in the middle: While I was taking a photo, my phone…
  • Two short actions, one after the other → past simple + past simple: When the sun came out, we walked by the river. (first the sun, then the walk)
  • Two long actions at the same time → while + past continuous: While Emma was talking, Jack was eating the cake.

Подсказка. Длинное действие (что происходило) — was / were + -ing; короткое, которое «врезалось» в него, — past simple. while ≈ «пока», when ≈ «когда (вдруг)».

  1. While we were walking to the first college, I into Anna.
  2. Anna for a bus when she saw us.
  3. While I was taking a photo, my phone out of battery.
  4. We back to the station when we got lost.
  5. When the sun came out, we by the river.
  6. What when you bumped into Anna?

Grammar Bank2Athe future: present continuous and be going to
formwhen?example
present continuousarrangement: the time and place are fixed, other people knowWe're meeting at Luigi's at seven. Dad's taking Gran for a walk.
be going to + verbplan, intention: I've decided, but nothing is bookedI'm going to bake a chocolate cake.
be going to + verbprediction: I can see it nowLook at those clouds! It's going to rain.
  • – and ?: We're not telling her. · I'm not going to tell anyone. · What are you doing on Saturday? · Are you going to make a toast?
  • Often both forms are possible: I'm seeing Anna tomorrow / I'm going to see Anna tomorrow. With a fixed time and other people, the present continuous is more natural.
  • With go we usually say I'm going to the party, not I'm going to go to the party.

Dad: And I promise I won't say a word to her. She thinks we're just going for a walk! 🤫

Grammar Bank2Awill or going to?
formwhen?example
will + verba decision now, at the moment of speakingWait — I know! We'll have it at our house.
will + verban offerI'll give you a hand. · Shall I move the sofa?
will + verba promiseI promise I won't say a word.
will + verba prediction — your opinion (I think, I'm sure, probably)I think Gran will love it.
be going toa plan — you decided beforeI'm going to bake a cake. (I decided last week.)
  • will not = won't /wəʊnt/.
  • Offers as questions: Shall I…? / Shall we…? — not Will I help you?
  • I think… + will: I think it'll be a great party. · I don't think he'll come.

Zoe's blog

9 min

a Now read Zoe's blog about her first shift. Find six words from the Vocabulary Bank. Was the day a disaster?

Zoe's blog · «My first shift»

Last summer I got my first job: I was a waitress at The Blue Wave, a little café by the beach. I had never worked before, so I was excited — and very nervous.

On the morning of my first shift, I opened my eyes, looked at the clock and realised it was ten past nine. My shift started at nine! I had overslept. My phone had run out of battery in the night, so my alarm hadn't gone off. I put on my uniform and rushed to the café without breakfast.

When I arrived, the café was already full of customers, and the manager, Rosa, was waiting for me at the door. She didn't look happy. «Table six,» she said. «Three hot chocolates. Quickly!»

I was carrying the hot chocolates to table six when I tripped over a bag. I spilt one all over a customer's white shirt! I apologised again and again. I was so embarrassed that my face went redder than the tomatoes in the kitchen.

But then something strange happened: the customer started laughing. It turned out that his daughter had filmed everything on her phone. That evening she posted the video online with the title «The Hot Chocolate Girl», and by the next morning it had gone viral.

When I came to work the next day, there was a long queue outside the café. Everyone wanted to meet the hot chocolate girl! I was panicking, but Rosa smiled and told me to calm down. In the end, my terrible first day turned out to be the best advert the café had ever had.

The blog post is about…

  5. The customer was angry and left. →
  6. The video went viral. →

narrative tenses

12 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. Every example is from Zoe's story. A good story needs three past tenses.Все примеры — из истории Зои.

Grammar Bank2Anarrative tenses: past simple · past continuous · past perfect
formuseexample
past simpleV2 / -edthe main events, one after anotherI put on my uniform and rushed to the café.
past continuouswas / were + -ingthe background; an action in progress when something happenedI was carrying the hot chocolates when I tripped.
past perfecthad + V3an earlier action: it happened before another past actionI realised I had overslept. My phone had run out of battery.
  • 'd = had: I'd overslept. Negative: hadn't + V3: My alarm hadn't gone off.
  • Use the past perfect only when you go back in time. Events in order → past simple: I woke up, got dressed and left.
  • V3 to remember: oversleep → overslept, run → run, go → gone, spill → spilt / spilled, see → seen.

Подсказка. В русском одно прошедшее время, а в английском рассказе видно, что случилось раньше: «Я поняла, что проспала» = I realised that I had overslept. Past continuous — фон («несла чашки»), past simple — события («споткнулась»), past perfect — шаг назад.

  1. When Zoe looked at the clock, she realised she .
  2. She the hot chocolates when she tripped over a bag.
  3. Her alarm didn't go off because her phone out of battery.
  4. When she arrived, Rosa for her at the door.
  5. The customer laughed. It turned out that his daughter everything.
  6. Zoe to the customer, cleaned the table and brought a new hot chocolate.

Radio: «Work Talk»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Host:Welcome back to «Work Talk». Last week we met people with unusual jobs. Today: first days at work. With me are Rosa, who runs a café by the beach, and Zoe, her youngest waitress. Rosa, what happened on Zoe's first day?
  2. Rosa, café manager:Well, it was a crazy morning. We had opened at eight, and by nine the café was already full. Two waiters had called in sick, so I was doing three jobs at once. And my new waitress wasn't there!
  3. Host:Zoe, what had happened?
  4. Zoe:I'd overslept! My phone had died in the night, so my alarm didn't go off. I woke up at ten past nine.
  5. Host:Had you ever worked in a café before?
  6. Zoe:No, never. I'd only done some babysitting. I'd watched lots of videos about how to carry three cups at once, but it's not the same in real life!
  7. Host:And then came the famous hot chocolate.
  8. Zoe:Yes. I was walking really fast, and I didn't see a bag on the floor.
  9. Rosa, café manager:When I saw the customer's shirt, I thought: that's it, he'll never come back.
  10. Host:But he did come back.
  11. Rosa, café manager:Yes, the next day, with his daughter. By the time they arrived, there was already a queue outside. Her video had got two million views overnight!
  12. Zoe:And I hadn't even seen it! I'd forgotten to charge my phone again, so my best friend came to my house to tell me.
  13. Host:Any advice for people who are starting their first job?
  14. Rosa, café manager:If you make a mistake, apologise, smile and keep going. Customers forgive mistakes. They don't forgive bad manners.
  15. Zoe:And charge your phone. Or buy a real alarm clock!

Rosa was doing three jobs at once because…

Grammar Bank2Apast perfect
formexample
+I / you / she / we / they had ('d) + V3I'd overslept. We had opened at eight.
–hadn't + V3I hadn't seen the video.

present continuous: now

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are from Daniel's call.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите. Все примеры — из звонка Дэниела.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаam / is / are + -ing
1
Одна мысль

Когда что-то происходит сейчас или в эти дни (now, today, this week), говорим: am / is / are + глагол-ing. «Дэниел стоит у школы (прямо сейчас)» → Daniel is standing. «Не» — not: I'm not teaching. В вопросе am / is / are идёт вперёд: Are you teaching?

2
Формула-конструктор
I+'m+standing+in front of the school.
They+'re+having+a break.

I → am (I'm) · he / she / it → is (he's, it's) · we / you / they → are (we're, they're)
-ing: teach → teaching · have → having (без e) · swim → swimming, sit → sitting

He+isn't+teaching+this week.
Are+you+having+a good time?

Короткий ответ: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. · Yes, they are. / No, they aren't. · Yes, it is. (не «Yes, it's»)

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊

  • He isn't teaching this week.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I standing. → ✅ I'm standing.
нужен помощник am / is / are
❌ She is play football. → ✅ She is playing football.
нужно -ing
❌ You are having a good time? → ✅ Are you having a good time?
в вопросе are — вперёд

Daniel's blog

7 min

a Daniel writes a blog for his school website. Read it. What is it about?Дэниел пишет блог для сайта своей школы. Прочитайте: о чём он?

Our week in St Petersburg

Hello from St Petersburg! This week ten of our pupils and I are visiting our partner school, and we're having a wonderful time.

At home in Manchester, I get up at half past six and go to school by bike. I teach five lessons a day, and I check homework every evening. But this week is different! I'm not teaching, and I'm not checking homework. I'm staying in a small hotel, and I'm walking to school — no bike!

Our pupils are staying with Russian host families. They're practising their Russian all day, and they're learning a lot. At this school, lessons start at half past eight, and the pupils stand up when a teacher comes in. Our pupils love it!

Right now I'm sitting in the staff room and writing this blog. My Russian colleagues are drinking tea and talking about the timetable. It's raining again, but we don't mind!

See you next week! — Mr Jones

usually or now?

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. The examples are from Daniel's blog.Прочитайте четыре шага. Повторите примеры из блога Дэниела.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаI teach or I'm teaching?
1
Одна мысль

Две «коробки». Обычно, всегда, каждый день → present simple: Daniel teaches five lessons a day. Сейчас, сегодня, на этой неделе → present continuous: This week he isn't teaching. Слова-подсказки помогают выбрать!

2
Формула-конструктор
He+teaches+Russian+every day.
This week+he+'s visiting+a partner school.

I teach: usually, always, often, never, every day, on Mondays
I'm teaching: now, right now, today, this week, at the moment, Look!

Do+you+teach+on Saturdays?
Are+you+teaching+this week?

Глаголы-«чувства» — без -ing: like, love, want, know. The pupils love it! (не are loving)

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Daniel usually goes to school by bike.
  • This week he's walking to school.
  • He checks homework every evening.
  • This week he isn't checking homework!
  • The pupils love St Petersburg.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I'm teaching Russian every day. → ✅ I teach Russian every day.
every day → present simple
❌ Look! It rains. → ✅ Look! It's raining.
сейчас → am / is / are + -ing
❌ I'm loving St Petersburg. → ✅ I love St Petersburg.
love, like, want, know — без -ing

  4. Tom:I get distracted all the time. I check my phone every five minutes, and I can't stay focused for more than ten minutes.
  5. Maya (coach):That's very common. Have you ever kept track of your time?
  6. Tom:No, never.
  7. Maya (coach):Then here's your first task. Keep track of your time for one week. Write down everything you do.
  8. Tom:Everything? Even social media?
  9. Maya (coach):Especially social media! And put your phone in another room while you're working.
  10. Tom:OK. What else?
  11. Maya (coach):Don't try to change everything at once. You can't break ten bad habits in one week. Set one goal and stick to it.
  12. Tom:And will that really work?
  13. Maya (coach):It will if you break big tasks down into small steps. Big tasks scare us; small steps don't. I'll call you next Friday to check you're on track.
  14. Tom:Great. I'm going to start tomorrow.
  15. Maya (coach):Tomorrow? Why not today?
  16. Tom:Ha! Fair point. I'm starting today.

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Tom's coaching session. When we report, the verb usually goes one step back into the past.

Grammar Bank2Breported statements
direct speechreported speechchange
«I get distracted.»He said (that) he got distracted.present simple → past simple
«I'm starting today.»He said he was starting that day.present continuous → past continuous
«I lost my biggest client.»He said he had lost his biggest client.past simple → past perfect
«I've never kept track of my time.»He said he had never kept track of his time.present perfect → past perfect
«I'll call you.»She said she would call him.will → would
«I can't stay focused.»He said he couldn't stay focused.can → could
«I'm going to start tomorrow.»He said he was going to start the next day.am going to → was going to
  • say something (to someone): She said (that)… · tell someone something: She told me (that)… — ✗ She said me.
  • Pronouns and time words change too: today → that day · tomorrow → the next day · next Friday → the following Friday · here → there.
  • If something is still true now, the verb can stay the same: She said big tasks scare us. In the exercises below, move the verb back.
  • that is optional: She told me (that) I was on track.

Подсказка. По-русски «Она сказала, что я молодец» — время не меняется. По-английски после said / told глагол обычно «сдвигается назад»: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could.

Tom's blog: week one

a A week later Maya calls Tom, as she promised. Tom writes about the call on his blog — in reported speech. Read. Is Tom on track?

Tom's blog · «Week one with a coach»

On Friday Maya called me, as she had promised. First she asked me if I had kept track of my time. I said I had, and I showed her my notes. The shock of the week: I had spent eleven hours on social media!

Maya didn't get angry. She asked me how I felt about it. I told her I was a bit embarrassed. Then she asked me where my phone had been while I was working. I admitted it had been on my desk, right next to my laptop.

So she gave me new instructions. She told me to put my phone in the kitchen, and she asked me to send her a photo of my desk every morning — with no phone on it! She also told me not to work for more than fifty minutes without a break.

At the end, I asked her when I would see results. She said it usually took about two months to form a new habit, but that I was already on track. Not bad for week one!

Is Tom on track after week one?

reported questions and instructions

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Tom's blog.

Grammar Bank2Breported questions and instructions
direct speechreported speech
yes / no question«Did you keep track of your time?»She asked me if (whether) I had kept track of my time.
wh- question«How do you feel about it?»
«When will I see results?»		She asked me how I felt about it.
I asked her when I would see results.
instruction«Put your phone in the kitchen.»
«Don't work for more than fifty minutes.»		She told me to put my phone in the kitchen.
She told me not to work for more than fifty minutes.
request«Can you send me a photo?» · «Please send me a photo.»She asked me to send her a photo.
  • A reported question is not a question any more: no do / did, statement word order, no question mark. ✗ She asked me how did I feel. ✓ She asked me how I felt.
  • Yes / no questions: if or whether.
  • Instructions: told + person + (not) to + verb. Requests: asked + person + to + verb. ✗ She told me don't work.

There's… It's… — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are from Anna's town.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите. Все примеры — из города Анны.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаThere's… It's…
1
Одна мысль

Сначала говорим, что ЕСТЬ (новое место): There's (There is) + a café. Потом говорим о нём — где оно, какое оно: уже It's (It is). Много вещей: There are two cafés → They're in the square. Вопрос «где?»: Where's the café? — It's next to the bank.

2
Формула-конструктор
There's+a café+in Market Street.
It's+next to+the bank.

Новое → There's a… · Уже знаем → It's… · Много → There are… → They're…

There are+two cafés+in the square.
They're+next to+the museum.
Where's+the café?+— It's+next to the bank.
3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊

  • There's a pharmacy. It's opposite the bus stop.
  • There are three museums. They're in the centre.
  • Where's the bus stop? — It's next to the museum.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There's a café. There's next to the bank. → ✅ There's a café. It's next to the bank.
Второй раз — уже It's.
❌ Where's the café? — Is next to the bank. → ✅ It's next to the bank.
Не забывайте It!
❌ Where is the shops? → ✅ Where are the shops?
Много → Where are…? — They're…

some / any — Grammar Easy

9 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. The examples are from the walk with Anna.Прочитайте четыре шага, слушайте и повторяйте. Примеры — из прогулки с Анной.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаsome / any
1
Одна мысль

Когда вещей много (shops, cafés), в обычном предложении (+) говорим some — «несколько, какие-то». В предложении с not (−) и в вопросе (?) — any. Одна вещь — как раньше, a: There isn't a cinema. Is there a market?

2
Формула-конструктор
There are+some+shops.
There aren't+any+cinemas.
Are there+any+restaurants?

+ → some · − и ? → any · Ответ: Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There are some nice shops in Bridge Street.
  • There aren't any cinemas.
  • Are there any good restaurants? — Yes, there are.
  • There are some lovely cakes at the market.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There are any shops. → ✅ There are some shops.
+ → some.
❌ There aren't some cinemas. → ✅ There aren't any cinemas.
− → any.
❌ Is there any cafés? → ✅ Are there any cafés?
Много → Are there…?

«Travel Talk» · Five questions for Kate, 26

Kate writes a travel blog. You may remember her story about a trip to Rome. This week she answered our questions.

How many countries have you been to?
Fourteen! I went abroad for the first time when I was nineteen — to Spain. I loved it, and I've travelled every year since then.

Have you ever been backpacking?
Yes, I have. Two years ago I went backpacking in Asia for three months. I stayed in hostels and met lots of amazing people.

Have you ever missed a flight?
Yes, twice! The first time was in Paris. I was buying souvenirs at the airport and I didn't hear the announcement. My plane took off without me!

What's the strangest food you've ever tried?
Fried insects in Thailand. A local gave them to me at a night market. They were crunchy — and not bad, actually!

Is there anything you've never done?
Lots of things! I've never been on a guided tour — I prefer to explore on my own and get lost. And I've never been to Portugal. But that's going to change: I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow!

Kate is…

present perfect: experiences

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Kate's interview.Примеры — из интервью Кейт.

Grammar Bank2Apresent perfect: ever / never → past simple for details
formexample
+I / you / we / they have ('ve) + V3 · he / she has ('s) + V3I've been to fourteen countries. She's tried fried insects.
–haven't / hasn't + V3 · 've never + V3I've never been to Portugal.
?Have / Has + person + ever + V3?Have you ever missed a flight? — Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
  • Experience (when? — not important) → present perfect. Details (when? where? what happened?) → past simple: Have you ever missed a flight? — Yes, I have. I missed a flight in Paris two years ago.
  • With yesterday, last year, in 2019, two years ago, when I was… → only past simple. ✗ I've been to Spain in 2019. ✓ I went to Spain in 2019.
  • been to = went and came back: She's been to Paris. · gone to = she is there now: She's gone to Lisbon.
  • V3: be → been, see → seen, eat → eaten, fly → flown, take → taken, meet → met, lose → lost, try → tried.

Подсказка. «Ты когда-нибудь…?» = Have you ever…? Опыт «вообще в жизни» — present perfect. Как только появляется «когда?» (ago, last, in 2019) — past simple.

  1. Kate to fourteen countries.
  2. you ever missed a flight?
  3. I been on a guided tour. I prefer to explore on my own.
  4. She in Asia two years ago.
  5. Have you ever tried fried insects? — Yes, I .
  6. He to Japan last year.

meaningwhere?example
justa very short time agohave + just + V3We've just landed.
alreadyit's done — maybe earlier than we expectedhave + already + V3I've already checked in.

a Listen to the radio phone-in «What Would You Do?». Ben calls the show with a dilemma. You will hear the new phrases — and some phrasal verbs from our last lesson! What is Ben's problem?Послушайте радиопередачу. Бен звонит со своей дилеммой. В чём его проблема?

Radio phone-in: «What Would You Do?»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Kate (host):Good evening and welcome to «What Would You Do?», the show where you call us with a problem and our listeners help you sort it out. Our first caller is Ben. Hi, Ben!
  2. Ben:Hi, Kate. Well, last week I bought an old sofa online. It was really cheap — only forty pounds. When I got it home, I found an envelope inside it. There was two thousand pounds in it!
  3. Kate (host):Wow! And what did you do?
  4. Ben:Nothing yet. I can't figure out what to do. Part of me says, «Keep it — nobody will find out.» But I feel guilty.
  5. Kate (host):Well, if I were you, I'd give it back. It isn't your money.
  6. Ben:I know, but the seller lives in a huge house. If I gave the money back, she probably wouldn't even notice!
  7. Kate (host):Let's hear from a listener. Lisa, you're on the air.
  8. Lisa:Hi, Ben. Something similar happened to me once. I found a wallet on a train and I handed it in at the station. A week later the owner found me and gave me a reward! And honestly, if you kept the money, you would feel terrible every time you sat on that sofa.
  9. Ben:Ha! That's true. But what if she asked me why I didn't call her earlier? I'd have to make up an excuse.
  10. Lisa:You don't need an excuse. Just tell her the truth. If I were in your shoes, I'd call her today.
  11. Kate (host):So, Ben, what are you going to do?
  12. Ben:OK, you're right. I'll do the right thing. If I find her phone number, I'll call her tomorrow. And if she doesn't answer, I'll go to her house.
  13. Kate (host):Great! Call us next week and tell us what happened.

What is Ben's problem?

second conditional

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are like Kate's and Lisa's advice. Look at the two colours: if + past, then would + verb.Прочитайте Grammar Bank. Две части: if + прошедшая форма, would + глагол.

Grammar Bank2Asecond conditional — imagined situations
IF + past formIf I found money,found · were · had · kept · could
,
would ('d) / wouldn't + verbI would give it back.I'd call · she'd feel · we wouldn't keep

Past form, but not past time! It is about now or the future — but it is imagined, not real.

❌ If I would find money, I would give it back.
❌ If I found money, I'll give it back.
❌ If I am you, I'll call her.
✅ If I found money, I would give it back. (no would after if!)
✅ If I found money, I'd give it back.
✅ If I were you, I'd call her. (advice)
  • Advice: If I were you, I'd… = «на твоём месте я бы…». If I was you is common in conversation, but were is better.
  • The if-part can come second — then no comma: I'd give it back if I found it.
  • Questions: What would you do if you found £2,000?

Подсказка. По-русски «бы» стоит в обеих частях: «Если бы я нашёл деньги, я бы их вернул». В английском would («бы») — только в одной части, а после if — прошедшая форма: If I found…, I would…

  1. If I two thousand pounds, I would give it back.
  2. If I were you, I her today.
  3. If you kept the money, you terrible.
  4. If I you, I would own up.
  5. She wouldn't make up an excuse if she the truth.
  6. What you do if you found a wallet?

a A week later Ben writes to the show. Did he do the right thing? What happened?Через неделю Бен пишет на радио. Что произошло?

From: Ben · To: «What Would You Do?»an email · about 170 words

Hi Kate, it's Ben — the man with the sofa! I want to tell you what happened. I found out the seller's name, Mrs Grant, from the website, and I called her. At first she didn't believe me! Then she started crying. The money was her husband's. He died two years ago, and she didn't know that he had hidden money in the sofa.

She was so happy that she gave me two hundred pounds as a thank-you present. I'm really glad I did the right thing. To be honest, if I found money again, I'd give it back straight away.

And now Mrs Grant has invited me for tea next Sunday. If the weather is nice, we'll sit in her garden and she'll show me her old photos. P.S. Thank you, Lisa! If I ever meet you, I'll buy you a coffee.

How to listen · Как слушать (5 правил — как в прошлый раз)
  1. Predict. Сначала картинки и вопросы — угадайте, о чём будет текст.
  2. Main idea first. В первый раз — только общий смысл. Не нужно понимать каждое слово!
  3. Key words. Во второй раз ищите ключевые слова: кто? что? где? когда?

a Rule 2 · Main idea. It's Monday. Ben tells Mia about his Saturday. Listen once. Don't read! Answer one question.Правило 2. Послушайте один раз без текста и ответьте на один вопрос.

Mia and Ben: Monday againListen for the main idea · Общий смысл
  1. Mia:Hi Ben! How was your weekend? Did you stay at home again?
  2. Ben:No, I didn't! It was great. On Saturday I went to Brighton with my brother Joe.
  3. Mia:Brighton! By car?
  4. Ben:No, we went by train. We got up really early and took the seven o'clock train.
  5. Mia:What did you do there?
  6. Ben:First we walked by the sea and took lots of photos. Then we had fish and chips on the beach.
  7. Mia:Did you swim?
  8. Ben:Yes, I did! The water was really cold. Joe didn't swim. He sat on the beach and ate an ice cream.
  9. Mia:Ha-ha! Did you buy anything?
  10. Ben:I bought a T-shirt for my sister. And guess what? We met my old school friend, Jake!
  11. Mia:What a nice surprise! When did you come home?
  12. Ben:We came home at ten in the evening. I was very tired, but it was a perfect day! What about you?
  13. Mia:Oh, I didn't go anywhere. I cleaned my flat and cooked dinner for my parents. Next time, take me with you!

How was Ben's Saturday?

irregular verbs — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are from Ben's day.Прочитайте четыре шага, слушайте и повторяйте. Все примеры — из дня Бена.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаPast Simple: irregular verbs
1
Одна мысль

Многие частые глаголы в прошедшем времени не берут -ed — они меняются: go → went, buy → bought. Их учим, как слова (карточки!). Хорошая новость: «нет» и вопрос — как в прошлый раз: didn't / Did + глагол в обычной форме: I didn't go. Did you go?

2
Формула-конструктор
I+went+to Brighton.
I+didn't+go+to London.
Did+you+go+to the sea?+— Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

go → went · get → got · have → had · see → saw · take → took · eat → ate · buy → bought · meet → met · swim → swam · come → came · sit → sat · lose → lost · find → found

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • We went to Brighton by train.
  • We had fish and chips on the beach.
  • Joe ate an ice cream.
  • Joe didn't swim.
  • Did you buy anything?
4
Осторожно!
❌ I goed to the sea. → ✅ I went to the sea.
go → went: учим, как слово.
❌ I didn't went. → ✅ I didn't go.
После didn't — обычная форма.
❌ Did you saw the sea? → ✅ Did you see the sea?
После Did — обычная форма.

  5. cook →
  6. eat →

  2. Ben:Good morning. I lost my phone on the train.

  5. Station assistant:Which train did you take?

  7. Station assistant:And where did you sit?

  12. Ben:Oh, fantastic! Thank you so much! When can I get it?
  13. Station assistant:We're open every day from nine to six.
  14. Ben:Great! I'll come tomorrow morning. Thank you!

Where did you go? — Grammar Easy

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat the questions.Прочитайте четыре шага. Повторите вопросы.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаWhere did you go?
1
Одна мысль

Вопрос о прошлом с вопросительным словом — как конструктор: вопросительное слово + did + you / he / she… + глагол в обычной форме. Did — маленький помощник прошлого, поэтому глагол уже без -ed и без went: Where did you go? What did you buy?

2
Формула-конструктор
Where+did+you+go?
What+did+Joe+eat?
When+did+they+come home?

Where? — где, куда · When? — когда · What? — что · Who? — кто, кого · What time? — во сколько · How? — как

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Where did you go? — To Brighton.
  • How did you get there? — By train.
  • What time did you come home? — At ten.
  • Who did you meet? — An old friend.
4
Осторожно!
❌ Where you went? → ✅ Where did you go?
Нужен помощник did.
❌ What did you bought? → ✅ What did you buy?
После did — обычная форма.
❌ When did come you home? → ✅ When did you come home?
Порядок: did + you + глагол.

b Step 1. Which question word? Look at the answer.Шаг 1. Какое вопросительное слово? Смотрите на ответ.

  1. did you go? — To the sea.
  2. did you meet? — My old friend Jake.
  3. did you eat? — Fish and chips.
  4. did you come home? — On Sunday evening.
  5. did you buy? — A T-shirt.
  6. did you go with? — With my brother.

c Step 2. Choose the right question.Шаг 2. Выберите правильный вопрос.

d Step 3. Write the question.Шаг 3. Напишите вопрос.

  1. (where / you / go) on Saturday?
  2. What (you / buy)?
  3. (what time / the train / leave)?
  4. Who (you / meet) in Brighton?
  5. (Joe / swim) in the sea?

e Step 4. Build the questions — you will ask your teacher in Speaking!Шаг 4. Соберите вопросы — вы зададите их преподавателю!

How to listen · Как слушать (5 правил — как в прошлые разы)
  1. Predict. Сначала картинки и вопросы — угадайте, о чём будет текст.

City Homes: a flat on Park RoadListen for the main idea · Общий смысл

  2. Mia:Hello! I'm calling about the flat on Park Road. Is it still free?
  3. Tom, the agent:Yes, it is. It's a lovely flat on the third floor, at number forty-two.
  4. Mia:How many bedrooms are there?
  5. Tom, the agent:There's one bedroom, a living room, a small kitchen and a bathroom. And there's a balcony!
  6. Mia:A balcony — great! Is there a washing machine?

  10. Mia:That's OK. I don't have a car. How much is the rent?
  11. Tom, the agent:It's six hundred and fifty pounds a month.
  12. Mia:Can I see the flat?
  13. Tom, the agent:Of course. Is Saturday at eleven OK?
  14. Mia:Yes, perfect. Thank you!

there is / there are — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are about Mia's new flat.Прочитайте четыре шага, слушайте и повторяйте. Все примеры — про новую квартиру Мии.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаthere is / there are · a / some / any
1
Одна мысль

Чтобы сказать, что где-то что-то есть, начинаем с There is (одна вещь) или There are (много). По-русски мы говорим «в кухне есть стол», а по-английски сначала There is, а место — в конце: There is a table in the kitchen. С одной вещью — a, с многими в «да» — some, в «нет» и вопросе — any.

2
Формула-конструктор
There+'s+a balcony.
There+are+some shops+near the flat.
There+isn't+a car park.
There+aren't+any curtains.
Is+there+a fridge?+— Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
Are+there+any shops?+— Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

is + a sofa, a fridge, a balcony · are + two chairs, some plants, any shops · some — в утверждении, any — в «нет» и в вопросе

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There's a balcony.
  • There are some shops near the flat.
  • There isn't a car park.
  • There aren't any curtains.
  • Is there a washing machine? — Yes, there is.
4
Осторожно!
❌ In the kitchen is a table. → ✅ There is a table in the kitchen.
Начинаем с There is, место — в конце.
❌ There is two bedrooms. → ✅ There are two bedrooms.
Много → are.
❌ There aren't some curtains. → ✅ There aren't any curtains.
В «нет» и в вопросе — any.

b Step 1. One or many? Choose is or are.Шаг 1. Одна вещь или много? is или are.

  1. There a sofa in the living room.
  2. There two windows in the bedroom.
  3. There some books on the shelf.
  4. There a lamp next to the bed.
  5. There some plants on the balcony.
  6. There a big mirror in the bathroom.

c Step 2. a, some or any?Шаг 2. a, some или any?

  1. There's fridge in the kitchen.
  2. There are chairs in the kitchen.
  3. There aren't curtains.
  4. Are there shops near here?
  5. There isn't desk in the bedroom.
  6. There are pictures on the wall.

d Step 3. Write. (+) yes · (−) no · (?) questionШаг 3. Напишите: (+) да, (−) нет, (?) вопрос.

  1. a balcony? — Yes, there is.
  2. any cupboards? — No, there aren't.
  3. (−) There any chairs in the living room.
  4. (−) There a TV in the bedroom.
  5. (+) a washing machine in the kitchen.

e Step 4. Build. Tap the words in the right order.Шаг 4. Соберите предложение.

f Step 5. About YOUR home. Two sentences.Шаг 5. Два предложения о вашем доме.

there was / there were — Grammar Easy

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat.Прочитайте четыре шага. Слушайте и повторяйте.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаthere was / there were
1
Одна мысль

Это то же самое there is / there are, только в прошлом. is → was, are → were. a / some / any — как раньше. Вопрос — просто меняем местами: Was there a balcony? Did здесь не нужен!

2
Формула-конструктор
There+was+only one chair.
There+were+two chairs+in the kitchen.
There+wasn't+a window.
There+weren't+any plants.
Was+there+a balcony?+— Yes, there was. / No, there wasn't.

сейчас: there is / there are → раньше: there was / there were

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • In my old flat there was only one chair.
  • There were two chairs in the old kitchen.
  • There wasn't a window in the kitchen.
  • Was there a balcony? — No, there wasn't.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There was two chairs. → ✅ There were two chairs.
Много → were.
❌ Did there was a balcony? → ✅ Was there a balcony?
Did не нужен: Was there…?
❌ There weren't some plants. → ✅ There weren't any plants.
В «нет» — any.

b Step 1. Choose.Шаг 1. Выберите.

  1. There a small table in my old kitchen.
  2. There two chairs.
  3. (−) There a sofa.
  4. (−) There any plants.
  5. (?) there a balcony in your old flat?
  6. (?) there any shops near it?

c Step 2. Now and before. Write was / were / wasn't / weren't.Шаг 2. Сейчас и раньше. Напишите was / were / wasn't / weren't.

  1. Now there is a balcony. In the old flat there a balcony.
  2. Now there are four chairs. In the old flat there two chairs.
  3. Now there are some plants. In the old flat there any plants.
  4. Now there is a sofa. In the old flat there a sofa.
  5. Now there is a big window in the kitchen. In the old kitchen there a window.

A New Chapter

Two years after moving to Edinburgh, Anna has set up a bakery. Starting again, a podcast and a blog — and the bridge from the past to now: for, since, ago, present perfect simple and continuous.

“Rome wasn't built in a day.”English proverb

  • tell the story of a new chapter in your life

  1. James (host):Welcome to «New Chapters», the podcast about people who start again. My guest today is Anna. She moved from Kazan to Edinburgh two years ago, and now she runs a small Russian bakery. Anna, welcome!
  2. Anna:Thanks, James! Sorry if I sound tired — I've been baking since five o'clock this morning.
  3. James (host):Five o'clock! So, what did you use to do in Kazan?
  4. Anna:I used to work in a bank. It was a good job, but I wasn't happy. When I moved here, I felt really homesick, and I missed my mum's pies. So I started baking them at home.
  5. James (host):And people liked them?
  6. Anna:They loved them! Then my neighbour asked me to make fifty pies for her wedding. That was the moment I decided to take a risk. I set up the bakery from scratch and opened it in April.
  7. James (host):So you've had the bakery for six months now. How's it going?
  8. Anna:Better than I expected! We don't advertise — it's all word of mouth. Some of our regulars have been coming every day since we opened.
  9. James (host):What's been the hardest thing?
  10. Anna:The early mornings! I still haven't got used to getting up at four. But all the hard work has paid off.
  11. James (host):And have you settled in? Have you made friends?
  12. Anna:Yes, I have. I've been taking Scottish dancing classes since January — that's where I've made most of my friends. And I keep in touch with my family every day. My mum has visited twice. She's tried every pie!
  13. James (host):I'm sure she approved! Anna, thank you so much.

The conversation is mainly about…

Babushka's Kitchen · Saturday, 3 p.m.

the call that never happened

12 min

a Now read a news article about a real-looking call that never happened. Find seven words from the Vocabulary Bank. Then answer: what is the article mainly about?

«The call that never happened»

Last month, a finance manager at a mid-sized logistics company in Manchester was tricked into sending two million pounds to criminals. The money has not been recovered, and the case is still being investigated by the police.

It all began with an email. The manager, who has not been named, was asked to join an urgent video call about a «confidential deal». On the call he could see the company's finance director and three other colleagues. Their faces were familiar and their voices were convincing — but every one of them was fake. The faces and voices had been generated by AI from videos that had been posted online after conferences and company events.

«I was taken in completely,» he told investigators. «They looked and sounded exactly like my colleagues.» During the call he was told to make fifteen payments to five different bank accounts. The scam was only discovered a week later, when he mentioned the deal to the real finance director.

Experts say the case shows how fast the technology is improving. Only a few years ago, deepfakes could be detected quite easily: the faces didn't blink, and the voices sounded robotic. Today a convincing fake can be made in a few hours with free software.

So what can be done? According to security specialists, large payments should always be verified through a second channel, such as a phone call to a known number. «If a request feels urgent and secret, that's the giveaway,» says one adviser. The company has since introduced new rules: from next month, no payment over ten thousand pounds will be made without a face-to-face check.

The article is mainly about…

the passive in all its forms

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. Most of the examples come from the article.

Grammar Bank2Athe passive — all forms
formactivepassive: be + V3
present simpleBanks check large payments.Large payments are checked.
present continuousThe police are investigating the case.The case is being investigated.
past simpleSomeone told him to pay.He was told to pay.
present perfectNobody has recovered the money.The money has not been recovered.
past perfectAI had generated the faces.The faces had been generated by AI.
futureThe company will make no payment…No payment will be made…
modalYou should verify payments.Payments should be verified.
infinitive / -ing—Nobody wants to be fooled. I hate being asked for passwords.
  • We use the passive when the doer is unknown, unimportant or obvious, and in news and reports. Add by + doer only if it is important: generated by AI.
  • Only the form of be changes; the main verb is always V3: is checked · was checked · has been checked · will be checked.
  • Informal English often uses get: He got fooled.

Подсказка. В русском часто «-ся» или «неопределённо-личная» форма: «Дело расследуется» = The case is being investigated; «Ему сказали» = He was told.

the expert view on Byte Size

a The story reached the tech podcast «Byte Size». Listen to Nina and Owen, an expert on online fraud. What is Owen's main message?

Podcast: «Byte Size»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Nina (host):Welcome to «Byte Size». Last month's deepfake video call is still all over the news. Owen, you study online fraud. How common are these scams?
  2. Owen:More common than people think. It's estimated that deepfake fraud has grown ten times in the last two years. And most cases are never reported, because companies are embarrassed.
  3. Nina (host):Who's behind them?
  4. Owen:Organised groups, mostly. The scammers in the Manchester case are believed to be based abroad, and they're thought to have used free software. Nothing cutting-edge, really.
  5. Nina (host):That's scary. And the manager is said to have been very experienced.
  6. Owen:Exactly, and that's the point. People say, «I would never be taken in.» But these fakes imitate faces, voices, even the way people move. It's not about being stupid. It's about trust.
  7. Nina (host):So how can we detect a deepfake?
  8. Owen:There used to be giveaways, like strange blinking or bad lip-sync. Those are disappearing. It's now thought that the best protection isn't a piece of technology, it's a process. If someone asks for money, hang up and call them back on a number you know.
  9. Nina (host):And will AI tools help?
  10. Owen:Some detection tools are said to be ninety per cent accurate. But don't rely on them completely. The criminals are using AI too.
  11. Nina (host):Owen, thank you. And listeners: if your boss asks for money on a video call, call them back first!

Owen's main message is that…

Grammar Bank2Ait is said that… · is believed to… · is thought to have…
patternexample
It + is said / believed / thought / reported / estimated / known + that + clauseIt's estimated that deepfake fraud has grown ten times.
person / thing + is said / believed / thought + to + infinitive (now)The scammers are believed to be based abroad.
person / thing + is said / believed / thought + to have + V3 (before now)They are thought to have used free software. The manager is said to have been very experienced.
  • Verbs: say, believe, think, report, know, expect, estimate, consider, claim.
  • Not ✗ The scammers are believed that they are abroad. → It is believed that the scammers are… / The scammers are believed to be…
  • Past reporting: It was thought that… · He was believed to be…

Подсказка. «Говорят, что…», «Считается, что…», «Полагают, что…» — информация без источника. Сейчас → to + глагол; раньше → to have + V3.

  5. The new tool is said ninety per cent of fakes.

Grammar Gym: modals of deduction

The salary spreadsheet has leaked at 2 a.m. Who did it — and how? Practise must / might / can't be and must / could / couldn't have done to crack the case.

B2HomeworkModals of deduction25–30 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

5 min
What to do
  1. Read the case file and the Grammar Bank.
  2. Do the quick-fire cards: is each sentence right or wrong?
  3. Then press «Далее» for the grammar practice.
Case file: the 2 a.m. leak. Remember Maria's company from the lesson? Now its salary spreadsheet has leaked to the whole office. Someone sent it from the account of Helen, the HR manager, at 2.13 a.m. Helen was at home with flu, and her laptop was in the office. Her password was on a sticky note under her keyboard. The cleaners work from 1 to 3 a.m. Only three people knew the file existed: Helen, the CEO and Victor, the CFO — and Victor resigned the next morning. Sam, a junior developer, raised the alarm. Help the security team find out what happened.

a Read the rules.

Grammar Bank1Amodals of deduction: present and past
how sure?presentpast
✅ I'm sure it's trueHe must be nervous.
He must be hiding something.		He must have known about the file.
🤔 It's possibleHe might / may / could be at his new job.
He might be talking to the press.		A cleaner might / may / could have seen the password.
❌ I'm sure it's not trueHelen can't be the leaker.Helen can't have sent it. = Helen couldn't have sent it.
  • Now, at this moment → modal + be + -ing: Sam's light is on. He must be checking the logs.
  • Past → modal + have + past participle: must have sent, might have seen, can't have known (not must has, not might have saw).
  • could have done = it's possible ✅ · couldn't have done = it's impossible ❌. One letter changes everything!
  • For "sure it's not true" use can't / couldn't, not mustn't.
  • In speech have is weak: must've /ˈmʌstəv/, might've /ˈmaɪtəv/, could've /ˈkʊdəv/. Never write must of.

Подсказка. must have done — «наверняка сделал», might / may / could have done — «возможно, сделал», can't / couldn't have done — «не мог сделать». Сейчас: must be doing — «наверняка сейчас делает».

b Right or wrong? Tap ✅ or ❌ for each sentence.

Someone must have used Helen's laptop.

Helen mustn't have sent the file — she was in bed with flu.

A cleaner might have seen the sticky note.

Victor must has known about the spreadsheet.

Sam's light is still on. He must be working late.

The leak can't have been an accident.

The attacker could have saw the password.

The message must have came from inside the company.

The story from the inside

10 min

a Listen to a podcast. A month after the ransomware attack, Hannah from Tech Brief talks to Mark Ellis, Brightwell's head of IT. Don't open the transcript until you have finished both tasks.

Podcast: «Tech Brief» — Brightwell, one month laterListen once for the story · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Transcript at the end
  1. Hannah (presenter):Welcome back to Tech Brief. A month ago, the online furniture retailer Brightwell was hit by a ransomware attack. Today we hear the story from the inside. Mark Ellis is Brightwell's head of IT. Mark, thanks for coming in.
  2. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):Thanks for having me. It isn't an easy story to tell, but I hope other companies can learn from our mistakes.
  3. Hannah (presenter):Take us back to that Friday night. When did you realise something was wrong?
  4. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):At about three in the morning, my phone rang. It was Jess, a junior engineer who was on call that night. She'd noticed strange traffic on our network, and she raised the alarm. By the time I'd logged in, thousands of files had already been encrypted.
  5. Hannah (presenter):What did you do first?
  6. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):Our first priority was to contain the attack, so we took the website and the warehouse systems offline. That stopped the ransomware from spreading, but it was a painful decision: no orders, no deliveries.
  7. Hannah (presenter):And when did the ransom note appear?
  8. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):In the morning, on every screen. They wanted four million dollars. We never seriously thought about paying, because we knew our backups were safe.
  9. Hannah (presenter):So how did the attackers get in?
  10. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):Two weeks earlier, one of our sales managers fell for a phishing email, and his account was compromised. The attackers used his password to log in to an old VPN server. That server had a known vulnerability. It should have been patched months earlier.
  11. Hannah (presenter):Wasn't the login protected by two-factor authentication?
  12. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):No, and that's the embarrassing part. When we moved our systems to the cloud last year, everybody forgot about that server. So the real root cause wasn't technical at all: nobody was responsible for it.
  13. Hannah (presenter):How long did it take to get back to normal?
  14. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):We restored everything from our backups, but it took five days. And five days of downtime is a very long time for an online shop.
  15. Hannah (presenter):And what about your customers?
  16. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):We found that the personal data of about twelve thousand customers had been copied, so it was a real data breach. We disclosed it to the regulator within seventy-two hours and contacted every customer ourselves. Being honest was the only option.
  17. Hannah (presenter):Finally, what's your advice for other IT teams?
  18. Mark Ellis (head of IT, Brightwell):Know what's on your network, keep it patched, and back up your data — and test your backups! A backup that you've never tested is just a hope.
  19. Hannah (presenter):Mark Ellis, thank you very much.

What to do · Что делать

a Read the rule. Past, present and future — all in Emma's week.Прочитайте правило.

Grammar BankHWEmma's week: past, present, future
formwhen?example
past simplefinished time: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019, when…?Emma met Jack eight years ago. When did you book the tickets?
present perfectpast → now, no exact time: ever, never, just, already, yet, for, sinceShe's lived in Brighton since 2019. Have you ever been to Oxford?
present simplehabits, routines: usually, always, every day, on FridaysEmma usually goes for a run before work.
present continuousnow, this week, temporary: now, at the moment, this weekThis week she's working from home.
present continuousfuture arrangement (time, people, tickets)She's meeting Lucy at nine on Saturday.
be going toplan (decided before) · prediction you can seeThey're going to walk by the river. Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
willdecision now · offer · promise · opinion (I think…)Then I'll take my umbrella. I think you'll love it.
  • for + a period (for eight years) · since + a point in time (since 2019). ago → only past simple.
  • like, love, know, want, need — no -ing: ✗ I'm knowing him ✓ I know him.

Подсказка. Есть «когда» (yesterday, last…, ago, in 2019) → past simple. Опыт или результат к сегодняшнему дню (ever, never, just, yet, for, since) → present perfect. Обычно → I do; сейчас / на этой неделе → I'm doing. Договорились → I'm meeting; решили заранее или видим признаки → going to; решаю сейчас, предлагаю, обещаю → I'll.

Grammar Gym: Then and Now

Lily is staying with her Gran this week. Practise what you know: Gran gets up at six · Right now she's making pancakes · Lily used to visit her every Sunday.

IntermediateHomeworkPresent simple vs continuous · used to25–30 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

5 min
What to do · Что делать
  1. Read the rule in the Grammar Bank. Press 🔊 and listen.Прочитайте правило, нажмите 🔊.
  2. Do the 8 quick cards: is the sentence right or wrong?Пройдите 8 карточек: верно или ошибка?

a Read the rule. Lily is staying with her Gran this week — all the sentences in this homework are about them.Прочитайте правило. Вся домашка — про Лили (из первого урока) и её бабушку.

Grammar BankHWPresent simple vs continuous · used to

Present Simple

habits, routines, facts
  • Gran gets up at six every day.
  • Lily doesn't eat meat.
  • Do you cook every day?
  • always, usually, often, never, every day, on Sundays

Present Continuous

right now · temporary, these days
  • Shh! Gran is sleeping.
  • This week Lily is staying with her Gran.
  • What are you cooking?
  • now, right now, at the moment, Look!, today, this week, these days

used to + verb

past habits and states — not true now
  • Lily used to visit Gran every Sunday.
  • She didn't use to like fish.
  • Did you use to cook with your mum?
Careful! State verbs are usually not in the Continuous: know, like, love, hate, want, need, understand, remember, think (= my opinion).
✗ I'm knowing this recipe. ✓ I know this recipe.   ✗ Gran is thinking it's too spicy. ✓ Gran thinks it's too spicy.

Подсказка. Спросите себя: это обычно / всегда / факт (Present Simple), сейчас / в этот период (Present Continuous) или раньше было, а теперь нет (used to)? В вопросе и отрицании — use to без -d: Did you use to…? I didn't use to… Глаголы состояния (know, like, want, need; think = «считаю») без -ing.

Grammar Gym 1A: From Night Owl to Early Bird

Lily the night owl is working early shifts at a café this month! Practise the grammar of lesson 1A: she usually wakes up at ten · this month she's working at seven · Look! She's making a cappuccino.

IntermediateHomeworkPresent simple vs continuous30–35 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: accuracyHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

6 min
What to do · Что делать
  1. Read the rule in the Grammar Bank 1A. Press 🔊 and listen.Прочитайте правило урока 1A, нажмите 🔊.
  2. Do the 8 quick cards: is the sentence right or wrong?Пройдите 8 карточек: верно или ошибка?
  3. Then go on: «Grammar», «Accuracy», «Challenge». Everything works on your phone.Потом — «Grammar», «Accuracy» и «Challenge». Всё можно делать с телефона, ответы сохраняются сами.

a Read the rule. Remember Lily, the night owl from our lesson? This month she is working early shifts at her friend Kate's café!Прочитайте правило. Помните Лили — «сову» из урока 1A? В этом месяце она работает в кафе подруги по утрам. Вся домашка — про неё.

Grammar Bank1APresent simple and present continuous

Present Simple

habits, routines, facts · always / usually
  • Lily usually wakes up at ten.
  • The café opens at seven.
  • She doesn't drink coffee in the evening.
  • Do you like early mornings? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Fridays, twice a week

Present Continuous

right now · temporary, these days
  • Look! Lily is making a cappuccino.
  • This month she's working at Kate's café.
  • She isn't sleeping late these days.
  • Are you enjoying it? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
  • now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!, today, this week, this month, these days
-ing: spellingexamples
most verbs + -ingwork → working, open → opening, study → studying
-e → -ingmake → making, write → writing
short verbs: double the last lettersit → sitting, get → getting, swim → swimming
-ie → -yinglie → lying, die → dying
always / usually / never go before the main verb, but after be: She always gets up at six. · She is always tired.
Careful! State verbs are usually not in the Continuous: know, like, love, hate, want, need, understand, agree, believe, remember.
✗ I'm knowing. ✓ I know.   ✗ I'm agree. ✓ I agree.
think and have have two meanings: I think it's great (= my opinion) · I'm thinking about a new job (= an action); She has a cat (= owns) · She's having breakfast (= an action).

Подсказка. Спросите себя: это обычно / всегда / факт (Present Simple) или прямо сейчас / в этот период (Present Continuous)? С he / she / it в Present Simple — -s, но после does / doesn't — без -s: Does she work? В вопросе нужен помощник: Where do you live? What are you reading? Глаголы состояния (know, like, agree…) — без -ing.

Confessions of a Morning Person

a blog post by Tom, 31

Hi, I'm Tom, and I'm a morning person. My alarm goes off at six, but I usually wake up before it. I make a cup of tea, put on my trainers and go for a run in the park. By eight I'm at my desk. I'm an architect, and I work best in the morning.

In the evening I take it easy. I don't watch much TV, and I never binge-watch series: I fall asleep after one episode! I usually read for half an hour, and I'm in bed by ten.

At the moment my life is a bit different. I'm training for my first half marathon, so I'm running more than usual and I'm eating a lot of pasta! My friend Lily, a real night owl, thinks I'm crazy. Maybe she's right.

Grammar Gym: there is / there are

A1–A2Homeworkthere is / there are25–30 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

5 min
What to do · Что делать
  1. Read the rule. Press 🔊 and repeat.Прочитайте правило. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите.
  2. Play «Right or wrong?».Сыграйте в «Верно или ошибка?».
  3. Then press «Далее» — more games!Потом нажмите «Далее» — там ещё игры!

a Read the rule about Anna's town. Tap 🔊.Правило на примерах из города Анны. Нажмите 🔊.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаthere is / there are: ➕ ➖ ❓
1
Одна мысль

Говорим, что где-то ЕСТЬ (или НЕТ): одна вещь → There is (a / an + слово), много вещей → There are (two, three… + слово-s). Нет → добавляем n't: There isn't / There aren't. Вопрос → меняем местами: Is there…? Are there…?

2
Формула-конструктор
There is+a café / an old library+in my street.
There are+two shops / three museums+in my street.

➖ There isn't a cinema. · There aren't many shops.

Is there+a park?+— Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
Are there+two cafés?+— Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

a café, a park — но an old library, an art shop (перед a, e, i, o, u → an).

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There is a little café in my street.
  • There are three museums in the centre.
  • There isn't a cinema.
  • Is there a park near your flat? — Yes, there is.
  • Are there many shops? — No, there aren't.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There is two shops. → ✅ There are two shops.
Две вещи → are.
❌ Are there a park? → ✅ Is there a park?
a park = одна вещь → Is there.
❌ Is there a bus stop? — Yes, it is. → ✅ Is there a bus stop? — Yes, there is.
Отвечаем теми же словами: there is.

b Right or wrong? Tap ✅ or ❌.Верно или ошибка? Нажмите ✅ или ❌.

There is a café in Anna's street.

There is two shops in her street.

There are a pharmacy next to the bank.

There are three museums in the centre.

Is there a cinema? — No, there isn't.

Are there a park near her flat?

There is an old library in the centre.

Are there two cafés in the square? — Yes, there is.

A2HomeworkPast Simple -ed25–30 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

7 min
What to do · Что делать
  1. Read the rule. Press 🔊 and repeat.Прочитайте правило, нажмите 🔊 и повторите.
  2. Do the quick cards: right or wrong?Пройдите карточки: верно или ошибка?
  3. Then go on to «Practice» and «Challenge». Everything is on your phone.Потом — «Practice» и «Challenge». Всё можно делать с телефона.

a Read the rule. Press 🔊 and repeat the examples.Прочитайте правило. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите примеры.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаPast Simple: regular verbs (-ed)
1
Одна мысль

We talk about the past → verb + -ed. · Рассказываем о том, что уже было (yesterday, last weekend, two days ago) — добавляем к глаголу -ed. Для всех одинаково: I, you, he, she, we, they — played.

2
Формула-конструктор
Mia+visited+her grandparents+last weekend.

Spelling · Как писать: play → played · like → liked (на -e: только d) · study → studied (согласная + y → ied) · stop → stopped (короткий глагол: удваиваем последнюю букву).

Нет → didn't + глагол без -ed. Вопрос → Did + кто + глагол без -ed:

Ben+didn't+walk+the dog.
Did+you+stay+at home?+— Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

Time words · Слова-подсказки: yesterday · last weekend / last Saturday · two days ago (ago — после: three days ago).

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Mia visited her grandparents.
  • They baked an apple cake.
  • It rained all weekend.
  • Ben didn't watch TV. He watched films!
  • Did Ben play computer games? Yes, he did.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I studyed English. → ✅ I studied English.
Согласная + y → ied. Но play → played (перед y гласная).
❌ The bus stoped. → ✅ The bus stopped.
stop, chat, plan — удваиваем последнюю букву.
❌ Did you watched a film? → ✅ Did you watch a film?
После Did — без -ed.
❌ I visited them before two days. → ✅ I visited them two days ago.
По-русски «два дня назад» → two days ago.

b Mia and Ben talk about their weekend. Is the sentence right or wrong? Tap.Миа и Бен рассказывают о выходных. Предложение верное или с ошибкой? Нажмите.

Last Saturday Mia visited her grandparents.

On Saturday Ben stayed at home and watch three films.

Mia didn't watched any films.

Did Ben play computer games on Sunday?

It rainned all weekend.

The number 42 bus stopped near Kate's house.

a Read the rule. Press 🔊 and repeat the examples.Прочитайте правило. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите примеры.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаPast Simple: irregular verbs · Where did you go?
1
Одна мысль

Many verbs don't take -ed — they change: go → went. · Многие глаголы в прошедшем не берут -ed — они меняются: go → went, see → saw. Их учим, как слова. «Нет» и вопрос — с помощником didn't / did, а глагол — в обычной форме: I didn't go. Did you go? Where did you go?

2
Формула-конструктор
Mia+went+to the seaside.
She+didn't+swim+in the sea.
Did+you+swim+in the sea?
Where+did+you+go?

go → went · see → saw · have → had · take → took · eat → ate · buy → bought · meet → met · come → came · get → got · swim → swam

Question words · Вопросительные слова: Where? — где, куда · When? — когда · What? — что · Who? — кто, кого · How? — как

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊

  • She took lots of photos.
  • She didn't swim in the sea.
  • What did she eat? — An ice cream.
  • When did she come home? — At eight.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I goed to the sea. → ✅ I went to the sea.
go → went: учим, как слово.
❌ I didn't went. → ✅ I didn't go.
После didn't — обычная форма.
❌ Did you saw the sea? → ✅ Did you see the sea?
После Did — обычная форма.
❌ Where you went? → ✅ Where did you go?
Нужен помощник did: Where + did + you + go.

Grammar Gym: Future Forms

Brightloop's chatbot Echo is getting ready for a Turing-style challenge. Practise will be doing, will have done and how sure you are: is bound to, may well, is unlikely to.

B1+ → B2HomeworkFuture continuous & future perfect25–30 min
Homework: ruleHomework: grammarHomework: challenge

Remember the rule

5 min
What to do
  1. Read the story and the Grammar Bank. Say the examples out loud with the short forms: we'll have trained.
  2. Do the «Right or wrong?» cards: is each sentence correct?
  3. Then press «Далее» — the practice is on the next page.
The story. Brightloop, a small software startup, is getting its AI chatbot Echo ready for the «Human or Bot?» challenge — a Turing test at a tech conference next Friday. Dana is the team lead, Leo is a developer and Mia tests everything. Their plans and predictions are your exercises.Одна история через всё задание. Каждый делает его по своей ссылке и отправляет сам.
Grammar BankHWfuture continuous · future perfect · how sure are you?
formuseexample
will be + -ing
future continuous		an action in progress at a moment in the futureThis time tomorrow, Leo will be presenting Echo to the investors.
Will you be + -ing…?a polite question about someone's plansWill you be using the test server tonight? I need to restart it.
will have + V3
future perfect		finished before a moment in the future: by Friday · by the time + presentBy the time the challenge starts, we'll have trained Echo on two million chats.

How sure are you? certain: will definitely · almost certain: is bound to, is likely to, will probably · quite possible: may well · possible: might, could · probably not: is unlikely to, probably won't

  • After by the time use the present: by the time the demo will start → by the time the demo starts.
  • be bound / likely / unlikely to + verb: Echo is bound to make a few mistakes. is bound to making · is likely make
  • Watch out: automation, not «automatization». In IT and business English the process is automation (test automation, the automation of customer support). Automatization is rare — mainly in psychology, for a skill that becomes automatic.

Подсказка. will be + -ing — «буду делать» в момент будущего (процесс); will have + V3 — «уже сделаю» к моменту (результат). by («к») почти всегда зовёт future perfect. «Автоматизация» в IT — automation.

a Right or wrong? Tap ✅ or ❌ for each sentence from Brightloop's team chat.

This time tomorrow, Leo will be presenting Echo to the investors.

By the time the demo will start, we'll have fixed the login bug.

By Friday, Mia will have tested every new feature.
